# package pcap

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/pcap"
```

Package pcap writes and reads capture files in the classic libpcap format with the Ethernet link type, so that traffic of the virtual network (and of the real backends) can be inspected with Wireshark or tshark.

## Constants

```go
const (

	// SnapLen is the largest frame stored.
	SnapLen = 65535
)
```

### type Writer

```go
type Writer struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Writer writes frames to a pcap file. It is safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewWriter

```go
func NewWriter(w io.Writer) (*Writer, error)
```

NewWriter writes the file header to w.

#### func (Writer) WriteFrame

```go
func (w *Writer) WriteFrame(t time.Time, frame []byte) error
```

WriteFrame writes one Ethernet frame captured at t. The classic format stores the seconds as an unsigned 32-bit count since 1970, so a t before 1970 or after 2106-02-07 06:28:15 UTC is refused with [profinet.ErrInvalidConfig](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-profinet#ErrInvalidConfig) instead of being written with a wrapped value. The original length of a frame of 2^32 octets or more is recorded as 2^32-1 (the frame itself is cut to SnapLen either way).
